summary.p: The Zinatu't-Tawárikh ("Ornament of Histories") compiled about 1218/1803-4 by Mírzá Muḥammad Ridá of Shaháwar for and by order of Fath-'Alí Sháh Qájár, in two volumes, not quite uniform in size. See Rieu's Persian Catalogue, pp. 135-136, and Aumer's Munich Catalogue, p. 79.

Vol. 1 comprises 412 ff. of 31'3 x 19'7 c. and 29 ll.; large, clear naskh with rubrications. A colophon on f. 100b gives the date 1288/1871-2, and another on f. 331 1289/1872-3; the latter adds that the MS. was copied by 'Ali Muḥammad ibn Muhammad Hasan for Mírzá Músà Mu'tamanu's-Sultán. This volume contains the Introduction (Aghda) and the first Piraya.
The contents of this history are as follows:
Introduction (Agház). On the creation of heaven and earth.

Piraya 1. On the great Prophets, Saints, Sages and Doctors, in two sections entitled Wajh, of which the second deals with the Prophet Muhammad and the first with his predecessors. Each of these sections comprises two subdivisions entitled Gina, the subjects of these being:
(ii) The Philosophers and Sages who preceded him (ff. 100-114).
(ii) The Prophet Muhammad and the Imáms who succeeded him (f. 114-2692).
(iv) The leading Divines and Doctors of Islám (f. 269-331). This last section comprises four subsections, treating of:
(1) The Relations and intimate Friends and Companions of the Prophet Muhammad and of the Imáms who succeeded him (ff. 269-289).
(2) Notable Divines, Doctors, Philosophers and Schoolmen of the Muslims, especially of the Shi'a (ff. 289–296).
(3) Notable Physicians, Astronomers and Mathematicians from the beginning of Islám to the time of writing (ff. 296-313).
(4) Poets, Gnostics and Metaphysicians, Persian and Arabian (ff. 313-331).

Here follows (ff. 333-342") an account of the Safawi Kings from the death of Sháh 'Abbás the Great and accession of Shah Şafí to the death of Shah Sultán Husayn, taken from the Zinatu't-Tawarikh of Mirzá Radí of Tabriz. The earlier history of the Safawis is omitted, says the author, because it is exhaustively treated in the Tarikh-i-Alam-árá-yi-Abbásí. The history of Nádir Sháh occupies ff. 342-343%, and is followed (ff. 343-411) by the history of the Qájárs down to the year 1218/1803-4.

The last three subsections (ff. 289-331) of the biographical portion of this work constitute its most interesting part, since they contain good and readable notices of many notable theologians and scholars of the Şafawi period, as well as of earlier Shi'a worthies.

handDesc.handNote: Large, clear naskh with rubrications. Copied by ʻAlī Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad Ḥasan علي محمد بن محمد حسن .

history.provenance: Copied by ʻAlī Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad Ḥasan for Mírzá Músà Mu'tamanu's-Sultánمیرزا موسی ملقب به موتمن‌السلطان. Part of the library of the late Sir A. Houtum-Schindler, purchased by me in January, 1917.
history.acquisition: Passed to Cambridge University Library in 1936 (the "Browne Bequest").

revisionDesc.change: Claude (auto-merge) Merged manual/ai/multi_match/G_16.1-G_16.2.xml (one AI file describing both volumes) into this record. That AI source interleaves both volumes' descriptions and mislabels the second volume's physical paragraph "Vol. 1" a second time; content was assigned to this volume (G. 16.1) by matching folio ranges and physical data (412 ff., 31.3 x 19.7 cm, 29 lines) against what was already fixed here (scribe ʻAlī Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad Ḥasan, origin 1289/1872-3) — the shared work-overview paragraph and everything covering ff. 1-411 went to this file; the "second volume" paragraphs went to G. 16.2 instead. Completed objectDesc/@form (was "other") and supportDesc/@material (was "chart") from the AI source; added layoutDesc/@writtenLines="29" (figure was already available, just not as an attribute); added handNote script="naskh" and description; added a provenance element (with @when) naming the patron Mírzá Músà Mu'tamanu's-Sultán, who has no existing authority key. Not yet reviewed by a cataloguer.
